# tote · v1.1.0

Source: https://tote.hexdocs.pm/

# tote

👜 Bags (or multisets) in Gleam

⚙️ This package works for both the Erlang and JavaScript target

## What’s a bag?

A `Bag` is a data structure similar to a set with the difference that it
can store multiple copies of the same item.

This means that you can efficiently check if an element is inside a bag with
the [contains](https://hexdocs.pm/tote/tote/bag.html#contains) function,
just like a set.
At the same time, you can ask how many copies of an item are contained inside a
bag using the [copies](https://hexdocs.pm/tote/tote/bag.html#copies) function.

If you are curious about implementation details, a

`Bag(a)`is nothing more than a handy wrapper around a`Map(a, Int)`that is used to keep track of the number of occurrences of each item.

## Installation

To add this package to your Gleam project:

```
gleam add tote
```
## Getting started

All the bag-related functions are in the `tote/bag` module, so once you’ve
imported that you’re good to go:

```
import gleam/int
import gleam/io
import tote/bag
pub fn main() {
  let valentino_bag =
    bag.from_list([
      "lipstick", "in", "my", "wh-", "wh-", "lipstick",
      "in", "my", "Valentino", "white", "bag", "?!"
    ])
  bag.copies(of: "lipstick", in: valentino_bag)
  |> int.to_string
  |> io.println
  // -> 2
}
```
If you don’t get the Valentino reference,
[you’re welcome!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzTlPjgJfTk)

## Contributing

If you think there’s any way to improve this package, or if you spot a bug don’t be afraid to open PRs, issues or requests of any kind! Any contribution is welcome 💜

---

# tote · v1.1.0

Source: https://tote.hexdocs.pm/index.html

# tote

👜 Bags (or multisets) in Gleam

⚙️ This package works for both the Erlang and JavaScript target

## What’s a bag?

A `Bag` is a data structure similar to a set with the difference that it

just like a set.

bag using the [copies](https://hexdocs.pm/tote/tote/bag.html#copies) function.

If you are curious about implementation details, a

`Bag(a)`is nothing more than a handy wrapper around a`Map(a, Int)`that is used to keep track of the number of occurrences of each item.

```

```

```
import gleam/int

      "lipstick", "in", "my", "wh-", "wh-", "lipstick",
```

# tote/bag · tote · v1.1.0

Source: https://tote.hexdocs.pm/tote/bag.html

This module has all the functions you may need to work with bags (if you
feel something is missing, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/giacomocavalieri/tote/issues))!

To quickly browse the documentation you can use this cheatsheet:

| Creating bags | [new](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#new),[from_list](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#from_list),[from_map](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#from_map) |
| Adding or removing items | [insert](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#insert),[remove](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#remove),[remove_all](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#remove_all),[update](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#update) |
| Querying the content of a bag | [copies](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#copies),[contains](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#contains),[is_empty](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#is_empty),[size](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#size) |
| Combining bags | [intersect](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#intersect),[merge](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#merge),[subtract](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#subtract) |
| Transforming the content of a bag | [fold](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#fold),[map](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#map),[filter](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#filter) |
| Converting a bag into other data structures | [to_list](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#to_list),[to_set](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#to_set),[to_map](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#to_map) |

A `Bag` is a data structure similar to a set with the difference that it
can store multiple copies of the same item.

This means that you can efficiently check if an element is inside a bag with
the [contains](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#contains) function, just like a set. At the same time, you
can ask how many copies of an item are contained inside a bag using the
[copies](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#copies) function.

If you are curious about implementation details, a

`Bag(a)`is nothing more than a handy wrapper around a`Map(a, Int)`that is used to keep track of the number of occurrences of each item.

`pub opaque type Bag(a)``pub fn contains(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), item: a) -> BoolReturns `True` if the bag contains at least a copy of the given item.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b"])
|> bag.contains("a")
// True
```
```
bag.from_list(["a", "b"])
|> bag.contains("c")
// False
```
`pub fn copies(in bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), of item: a) -> IntCounts the number of copies of an item inside a bag.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "c"])
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 2
```
```
pub fn filter(
  bag:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  keeping predicate: fn(a, Int) -> Bool,
) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Only keeps the items of a bag the respect a given predicate that takes as input an item and the number of its copies.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "b", "c", "d"])
|> bag.filter(keeping: fn(_, copies) { copies <= 1 })
|> bag.to_list
// [#("c", 1), #("d", 1)]
```
```
pub fn fold(
  over bag:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  from initial: acc,
  with fun: fn(acc, a, Int) -> acc,
) -> accCombines all items of a bag into a single value by calling a given function on each one.

The function will receive as input the accumulator, the item and its number of copies.

## Examples

```
let bag = bag.from_list(["a", "b", "b"])
bag.fold(over: bag, from: 0, with: fn(count, _, copies) {
  count + copies
})
// 3
```
`pub fn from_list(list: List(a)) -> `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Creates a new bag from the given list by counting its items.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "c"])
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 2), #("b", 1), #("c", 1)]
```
`pub fn from_map(map: `[dict.Dict](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_stdlib/1.0.0/gleam/dict.html#Dict)(a, Int)) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Creates a new bag from the map where each key/value pair is turned into an item with those many copies inside the bag.

## Examples

```
map.from_list([#("a", 1), #("b", 2)])
|> bag.from_map
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 1), #("b", 2)]
```
```
pub fn insert(
  into bag:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  copies to_add: Int,
  of item: a,
) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Adds `n` copies of the given item into a bag.

If the number of copies to add is negative, then this is the same as calling
[ remove](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#remove) and will remove that many copies from the bag.

## Examples

```
bag.new()
|> bag.insert(2, "a")
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 2
```
```
bag.from_list(["a"])
|> bag.insert(-1, "a")
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 0
```
`pub fn intersect(one: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), with other: [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Intersects two bags keeping the minimum number of copies of each item that appear in both bags.

## Examples

```
let bag1 = bag.from_list(["a", "a", "b", "c"])
let bag2 = bag.from_list(["a", "c", "c"])
bag.intersect(bag1, bag2)
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 1), #("c", 1)]
```
`pub fn is_empty(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> BoolReturns `True` if the bag is empty.

⚠️ This is more efficient than checking if the bag’s size is 0. You should always use this function to check that a bag is empty!

## Examples

```
bag.new()
|> bag.is_empty()
// True
```
```
bag.from_list(["a", "b"])
|> bag.is_empty()
// False
```
`pub fn map(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), with fun: fn(a, Int) -> b) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(b)Updates all values of a bag calling on each a function that takes as argument the item and its number of copies.

If one or more items are mapped to the same item, their occurrences are summed up.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "b"])
|> bag.map(fn(item, _) { "c" })
|> bag.to_list
// [#("c", 3)]
```
`pub fn merge(one: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), with other: [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Adds all the items of two bags together.

## Examples

```
let bag1 = bag.from_list(["a", "b"])
let bag2 = bag.from_list(["b", "c"])
bag.merge(bag1, bag2)
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 1), #("b", 2), #("c", 1)]
```
```
pub fn remove(
  from bag:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  copies to_remove: Int,
  of item: a,
) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Removes `n` copies of the given item from a bag.

If the quantity to remove is greater than the number of copies in the bag, all copies of that item are removed.

⚠️ Giving a negative quantity to remove doesn’t really make sense, so the sign of the

`copies`argument is always ignored.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "a"])
|> bag.remove(1, "a")
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 1
```
```
bag.from_list(["a", "a"])
|> bag.remove(-1, "a")
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 1
```
```
bag.from_list(["a", "a"])
|> bag.remove(10, "a")
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 0
```
`pub fn remove_all(from bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a), copies_of item: a) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Removes all the copies of a given item from a bag.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a"])
|> bag.remove_all("a")
|> bag.to_list
// [#(b, 1)]
```
`pub fn size(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> IntReturns the total number of items inside a bag.

⚠️ This function takes linear time in the number of distinct items in the bag.

If you need to check that a bag is empty, you should always use the

[function instead of checking if the size is 0. It’s going to be way more efficient!](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#is_empty)`is_empty`

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "c"])
|> bag.size
// 4
```
```
pub fn subtract(
  from one:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  items_of other: [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Removes all items of the second bag from the first one.

## Examples

```
let bag1 = bag.from_list(["a", "b", "b"])
let bag2 = bag.from_list(["b", "c"])
bag.subtract(from: one, items_of: other)
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 1), #("b", 1)]
```
`pub fn to_list(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> List(#(a, Int))Turns a `Bag` into a list of items and their respective number of copies in
the bag.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "c"])
|> bag.to_list
// [#("a", 2), #("b", 1), #("c", 1)]
```
`pub fn to_map(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> [dict.Dict](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_stdlib/1.0.0/gleam/dict.html#Dict)(a, Int)Turns a `Bag` into a map. Each item in the bag becomes a key and the
associated value is the number of its copies in the bag.

`pub fn to_set(bag: `[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)) -> [set.Set](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_stdlib/1.0.0/gleam/set.html#Set)(a)Turns a `Bag` into a set of its items, losing all information on their
number of copies.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a", "b", "a", "c"])
|> bag.to_set
// set.from_list(["a", "b", "c"])
```
```
pub fn update(
  in bag:
```
[Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a),
  item item: a,
  with fun: fn(Int) -> Int,
) -> [Bag](https://tote.hexdocs.pm#Bag)(a)Updates the number of copies of an item in the bag.

If the function returns 0 or a negative number, the item is removed from the bag.

## Examples

```
bag.from_list(["a"])
|> bag.update("a", fn(n) { n + 1 })
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 2
```
```
bag.new()
|> bag.update("a", fn(_) { 10 })
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 10
```
```
bag.from_list(["a"])
|> bag.update("a", fn(_) { -1 })
|> bag.copies(of: "a")
// 0
```
